title: Leader election
short: Pick exactly one node to be in charge, and a new one if it dies.
what: Some jobs need exactly one boss: the node that accepts writes, or the one that runs the nightly job. Leader election lets a group of nodes agree on who that is. If the leader stops sending heartbeats, the others vote, and whoever gets a majority becomes the new leader.
analogy: A team picking a captain. If the captain goes home sick, the team votes again, and you need more than half the votes to win.

frames.say: Five database nodes. A leads term 1: it takes all writes and sends a heartbeat every 100 ms to say it's alive.
A crashes and the heartbeats stop. Each follower waits a random 150-300 ms before acting, so they rarely all act at once.
C's timer runs out first, at 170 ms. It starts term 2, votes for itself, and asks every other node for a vote.
B, D and E haven't voted in term 2 yet, so each says yes. A node gives one vote per term, so two winners are impossible.
C has 4 of 5 votes. More than half is enough, so C is the leader for term 2 and starts sending heartbeats.
A restarts, still thinking it leads term 1. Its messages carry term 1, lower than 2, so they're rejected and A becomes a follower.

when: Only one node may accept writes
A job must run once, not on every server
Replicas must agree which one is primary
Fail over when the main node dies
python:
nodes = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]
alive = {"B", "C", "D", "E"}                            # A, the old leader, crashed
timeouts = {"B": 240, "C": 170, "D": 290, "E": 205}     # ms, picked at random
voted_in = {n: 1 for n in nodes}                        # last term each node voted in

term = 2
candidate = min(alive, key=timeouts.get)                # first timer to run out
votes = [candidate]                                     # it votes for itself
for n in sorted(alive - {candidate}):
    if voted_in[n] < term:                              # one vote per term
        voted_in[n] = term
        votes.append(n)
print(candidate, "asks for votes in term", term, "->", votes)
print("leader!" if len(votes) > len(nodes) // 2 else "no majority, try again")
print("message from A in term 1 accepted?", 1 >= term)
output:
C asks for votes in term 2 -> ['C', 'B', 'D', 'E']
leader!
message from A in term 1 accepted? False
watch: Use an odd number of nodes, 3 or 5. Four nodes survive no more failures than three.
An old leader must be fenced off by its term number, or two leaders write at once (split brain).
Don't write your own: use ZooKeeper, etcd, or your database's built-in election.
interview: Design a job scheduler that runs each job exactly once
Design a replicated log like Kafka
